title: Build for AnyCPU instead of hardcoded x64
paragraphs: All four .NET projects pinned PlatformTarget to x64, so the built task-stats.dll could not be loaded by the .NET runtime on a Windows ARM64 machine that only has the ARM64 runtime installed (dotnet threw "The assembly architecture is not compatible with the current process architecture", and run-unit-tests.bat failed with "You must install .NET to run this application"). AnyCPU lets the JIT produce native code for whatever architecture the host process actually is, which still builds and runs the same way on x64 Windows (verified via CI) and now also runs on Windows on ARM.

title: looking good
taskmon: embed into taskbar, fix hit testing, improve graph rendering
paragraphs:
Embed into taskbar:
- Set WS_CHILD and parent the overlay to Shell_TrayWnd instead of floating on top of the taskbar.
- Switch from UpdateLayeredWindow (which has issues with WS_CHILD) to standard WM_PAINT.
- Use LWA_COLORKEY with a near-black background (RGB 16, 16, 16) to make it perfectly transparent while seamlessly blending anti-aliased text into the dark taskbar.

Fix hit testing:
- Transparent keyed pixels fall through standard Windows hit testing.
- Add a Low-Level Mouse Hook (WH_MOUSE_LL) to intercept clicks within the overlay bounds and manually trigger the context menu or resource monitor.

Improve graph rendering:
- Cap sparklines to leave a 14px safe zone at the top, preventing 100% spikes from overlapping the label text.
- Remove drop shadows from top-row text to make it crisper against the dark background (kept for center-body values like GPU temp).

title: taskmon: move values into label row, shorten net labels
paragraphs: All sections now show a short label left and live value right in the header row, with a clean sparkline filling the body below.

- CPU per-core grid: left-align the CPU label (was centered), add total CPU% right-aligned in the same row
- CPU aggregate, GPU, MEM: same label-left / value-right treatment; remove the large bold value from the graph body
- GPU: when both util and temp are enabled, util% goes in the header and temp stays in the body (only one value fits the header row)
- NET: rename UPLOAD/DOWNLOAD to UP/DL, move speed value into header row

title: fix taskmon covering the system tray chevron on Win11 22H2+
paragraphs: On Win11 22H2+, the show hidden icons overflow button moved from being a child of TrayNotifyWnd to a direct child of Shell_TrayWnd. The old lookup found nothing and fell back to TrayNotifyWnd.Left, which did not account for the chevron sitting just to its left.
Now enumerate Button children of both TrayNotifyWnd and Shell_TrayWnd, taking the leftmost one that sits to the left of TrayNotifyWnd.
